solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Germany's head needs to give approval, please

indicators.note: the head of something is its top or front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the country's name
to ratify is to give formal approval to a treaty or decision

explanation.surface: Germany's leader is asked, politely, to sign off on some agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 'please' reads as a polite request tacked on, but it is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to give them satisfaction, which is exactly what the verb means: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Take all the hardships from rugged sex

parts.note: rugged ground or features are rough
'it' is a coy crossword word for sex, as in 'doing it'

explanation.surface: Someone endures every hardship that comes from a bout of rough lovemaking.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex is a long-standing crossword convention; 'rugged sex' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means living without comforts, putting up with hardship, as when camping in the wild.

clue.text: Wife who wears the trousers ready for your viewing pleasure?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the thing rather than a noun synonym

parts.note: TV is short for transvestite, someone who dresses in clothes of the other sex
'ready, steady, go' or 'get set': set means prepared

explanation.surface: A domineering wife is all prepared to put on a show for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wears the trousers' usually means bossy, but here it is taken literally: a wife in men's trousers is cross-dressing, a TV. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A television receiver exists to provide entertainment you watch, so it is the object of your viewing pleasure.

clue.text: Confronted daft couple screwing (no latitude shown)

indicators.note: screwing twists things round, so the letters are wrung into a new order
'no' says a letter is absent, so the thing it names is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for latitude on maps

explanation.surface: A silly pair are caught in the act, with the bracket hinting nobody gave them any leeway.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the L from DAFT COUPLE, then rearrange the remaining nine letters; 'shown' just completes the bracketed phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To face up to something is to confront it squarely rather than avoid it, so the phrasal verb matches the past tense.

clue.text: Some fear a fatuous ex-leader

indicators.note: 'some' takes only part of what follows, so the letters lie within the run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A silly former leader is regarded with some fear.
explanation.walkthrough: Yasser Arafat led the Palestine Liberation Organization until his death in 2004.
explanation.definitionFit: Yasser Arafat, long-time PLO chairman and Palestinian president, is a former leader by example.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory Republican circle? Yep, dodgy

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letter O is round like a circle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sceptic shrugs off a Republican inner circle as shady.
explanation.walkthrough: Ropey is informal British English for poor or shoddy, as in feeling ropey after a late night.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropey is a colloquial British adjective meaning of poor quality, a near synonym of unsatisfactory.

clue.text: Wretched alien UFO fellow

indicators.note: alien means strange and foreign, so the letters take on an unfamiliar arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miserable extraterrestrial chap stands beside his flying saucer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' sits naturally beside 'UFO' as part of the sci-fi picture, which hides its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wretched is deeply unhappy, and the phrase describes a person brimming with sorrow: a plain synonym.

clue.text: Hard going, old Liberal leader — party attack

indicators.note: something going is departing, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: Jeremy Thorpe led the British Liberal Party from 1967 to 1976
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A former Liberal leader struggles as his party comes under assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard going' looks like one phrase for difficulty, but splits into H and a signal to remove it from THORPE, the scandal-hit 1970s Liberal leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo something is to wreck or sink it deliberately, so as a verb it means to attack.

clue.text: Reserved — but succeeded in having sex, with time for cocaine

indicators.note: 'X for Y' means one thing is swapped in where the other stood

parts.note: to score is slang both for succeeding and for getting someone into bed
T is the abbreviation for time
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A shy person nevertheless got lucky, and swapped the drugs for a quieter time.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the C in SCORED with T. 'Reserved' looks like a description of a shy person but means kept aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods reserved for later are kept back or put away, the same sense as kept in storage.

clue.text: "Pushover" sexualised females act otherwise

parts.note: a vulgar slang term for women viewed sexually

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so these letters are put in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Women portrayed in a sexualised way behave contrary to expectation, defying the label of easy target.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks set the definition apart; the rest builds the word from crude slang plus a rearranged three-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pussycat is informal for a gentle, easily handled person, so it is a soft touch or pushover.

clue.text: Liberal party crushes Left, which is mean

indicators.note: to crush is to squeeze something in, so one piece is pressed inside another
liberal means free and loose, so the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A political party of liberals squashes its left wing, which seems petty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal party' reads as the Liberals, but 'Liberal' is the signal to rearrange the second word before it takes in L.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean here is the adjective for stingy or meagre, and paltry describes an amount that is small and contemptible.

clue.text: see 18dn.
Criminal's ready, being blue and tender?

parts.note: blue jokes or films are smutty
legal tender is money

explanation.surface: A villain is all set to go, though feeling sad and sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for cash (the readies), and 'blue' and 'tender' pose as feelings before turning out to mean smutty and currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicitly gained cash belonging to a crook is the sense: ready money from crime, hence tainted funds.

clue.text: Was a physical disciplinarian cash-deficient?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: beat someone with a leather strap as punishment

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stern corporal punisher was also short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a past-tense verb, the second an adjective; the one word covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Being strapped for cash is a common idiom for being hard up, while to strap a pupil was to thrash them.

clue.text: Nothing but opposing members, which is awkward

parts.note: 'all' can mean entirely, as in 'all talk'
thumbs are the opposable digits, members of the hand

explanation.surface: A parliament filled only with opposition members makes for a clumsy situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' suggests MPs and 'opposing' the opposition benches, but the members are digits and opposing means opposable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone clumsy with their hands, as if every finger were a thick digit: awkward.

clue.text: Unreliable erection likely from this western type?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of a rogue builder rather than a straight synonym
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dodgy, unqualified tradesman whose buildings are shoddy
second meaning: the cattle-herding hero of a Western film

explanation.surface: A smutty joke about a man prone to unreliable erections, dressed up as a film genre.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a cowboy is a rogue tradesman, so a cowboy builder's erection, meaning a building, is likely to be shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the Wild West cattle hand of Western films and, in British slang, an incompetent or dishonest builder.

clue.text: Meghan Markle's second PC outburst with which she'll get toasted no doubt

definitions.text: with which she'll get toasted no doubt
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the drink rather than a noun

indicators.note: an outburst throws everything out in disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the word

parts.note: the letter in second place of the surname
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Duchess of Sussex makes a politically correct outburst, yet she will be toasted at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Markle's second' looks like a second outburst by her; it is the A in her surname. 'Toasted' means honoured with raised glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the sparkling wine traditionally poured to toast a royal or a bride at celebrations.

clue.text: A test of public opinion by Corbyn's no. 2 — "God!"

parts.note: a poll is a survey of public opinion

indicators.note: number two picks the letter standing second in the word

parts.note: the letter in second place of the name

explanation.surface: A survey of voters puts the former Labour leader's deputy in charge, and someone exclaims in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 2' reads as Jeremy Corbyn's deputy; it is his name's second letter. 'God!' is an exclamation in the surface but the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is the Greek and Roman deity of music, light and prophecy, so an example of a god.

clue.text: (& 12ac.) Hairstyle feature's very fashionable — the last word?

parts.note: the line where hair is divided
the possessive ending supplies its letter
hot means very much in vogue

explanation.surface: A stylist asks whether a particular feature of a haircut is the latest thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is not a possessive but a letter in its own right, joining the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark delivered on leaving that settles an argument is having the final say, so the idiom means the last word.

clue.text: Trump approach to world economics has Washington in clutches of stock exchange member

indicators.note: something held in the clutches of another is gripped inside it

parts.note: a trader buys and sells on the exchange
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: Trump's protectionist economics leaves Washington at the mercy of a Wall Street dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a long descriptive phrase fitting Donald Trump's tariff battles with China.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump imposed tariffs and invited retaliation, so his global economic policy was a conflict fought through trade.

clue.text: Top Tory source right in trouble

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it

parts.note: crude slang for trouble, as in 'in the shit'
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A senior Conservative informant reports that the right wing is in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Tory' looks like a senior Conservative, but 'Top' is the garment definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A top is any garment for the upper body, and a short-sleeved cotton shirt with no collar is an example.

clue.text: Agreeable getting end away? With stupid git on top, it could be the death of you

definitions.text: it could be the death of you

indicators.note: 'end away' sends the final letter off, so it is cut from the word

parts.note: an arse is British slang for a fool
agreeable means pleasant, nice

explanation.surface: A pleasant fellow gets lucky in bed, but with an idiot on top things could turn fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting your end away' is British slang for having sex; here it simply strips a last letter. In a down clue, 'on top' puts one piece above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a notorious poison, so a deadly substance that could kill whoever swallows it.

clue.text: Clergyman chief bound to welcome those not sexually discriminating

indicators.note: to welcome is to take a guest in, so one piece receives another inside

parts.note: arch- means chief, as in archenemy
a bound is a leap or hop
bis is short for bisexuals, attracted to both sexes

explanation.surface: A senior churchman is obliged to accept people of all sexual orientations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'obliged to', but 'bound' is a leap and 'to welcome' is the instruction to take in the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop is a senior bishop in charge of a province, so a high-ranking member of the clergy.

clue.text: (& 23ac.) Pants he brandished, interrupting sex earlier

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: 'it' is a coy crossword word for sex

indicators.note: brandished means waved about wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man waved his underwear about, breaking off from lovemaking a while ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as either underwear or a British word for rubbish, but here its letters are part of the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done earlier happened at a previous time, so it took place before now: a phrase synonym.

clue.text: see 22dn.
Turning up with politicians, shakes hands enthusiastically

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way

parts.note: taken as written
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone arrives among politicians, greeting them with vigorous handshakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' looks like arriving, but it instructs that the little word be flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone's hand is to shake it with vigour, working it up and down like a pump handle.

clue.text: Lot gets me kit off outside back of Harrods

indicators.note: being outside means surrounding something else
something off is wrong or awry, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the back of something is its end, so the final letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the store's name

explanation.surface: A man strips off outside the back of a famous London department store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kit off' is British slang for undressing; Harrods is a luxury London store. 'Lot' means one's fate, not a quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is fate or destiny, from Turkish, and one's lot in life is the fortune that destiny allots.

clue.text: Fighting unit deviously met Nigel (having changed political sides)

indicators.note: acting deviously means taking a crooked route, so the letters are twisted out of order
having changed means one thing has been exchanged for another, so a letter is swapped

parts.note: taken as written
the two political sides are left and right, L and R; the right comes in where the left stood

explanation.surface: Someone secretly met Nigel Farage after he defected, plotting some campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L (left) in NIGEL for R (right), then rearrange the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a permanent unit of an army, typically several battalions, so a military fighting unit.

clue.text: Guest's potty which fits under genitals?

definitions.note: a descriptive clause for the thing rather than a noun

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters go mad and change order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A visitor's chamber pot sits snugly below his private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' plays on the child's chamber pot, which also sits under the genitals, but it is the signal word. A gusset is the reinforcing panel in the crotch of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusset is the fabric panel sewn into the crotch of knickers or tights, which sits beneath the genitals.

clue.text: Designer gives some lovers a certificate

indicators.note: 'some' takes only part of what follows, so the letters lie within the run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A fashion designer hands certain couples a document of recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: Gianni Versace founded the Italian fashion house that bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gianni and Donatella Versace are Italian fashion designers, and the brand name stands for the designer by example.
